# Perspective-coupled projective erosion and an exact neutrality obstruction

This note realizes the ordinary projective boundary weight through a
genuine tight midpoint contact for arbitrary convex bodies. Weighted
Jensen gives exact finite-time compatibility, not merely a formal contact
inequality. The input costs and cap losses are retained. A centroid-source
calibration shows that this particular compatible coupling can be entirely
neutral, even when its own-fiber efficiency exceeds the mixed normalized
depth. No universal cost bound or OC conclusion is asserted.

## 1. Data and an explicit interior-midpoint premise

Let A,B,K be positive convex bodies in R^d, d>=1, with

    M=(A+B)/2 subset K.

Choose interior points y_A in A and y_B in B and put y=(y_A+y_B)/2.
Thus y is interior to M and K. Translate each body by its indicated
center and temporarily use A,B,M,K for the centered bodies. Their support
functions are positive and satisfy

    h_M(n)=[h_A(n)+h_B(n)]/2<=h_K(n).                        (1)

For a prescribed y this construction assumes y belongs to int M.
It does not infer that fact from deepestness or from compatibility.
Interior points of M admit such interior endpoint decompositions:
int(A+B)=int A+int B. One elementary proof is to start with interior
endpoint points, express a small outward continuation beyond the chosen
interior sum as a point of A+B, and interpolate toward those fixed
interior points. Conversely every sum of interior endpoint points is
interior to the Minkowski sum.

Take the actual projective normalization of K about y from
`candidate 2d9458b5433d0a83`: choose a such that
1+a.x>0 on K and T_a(K), T_a(x)=x/(1+a.x), has centroid zero. Let f be
the positive finite convex extension of t^(-d) defined in
`candidate 4e871da0351ca07a`.
Its values and first derivative are bounded on every compact interval.

The desired source erosion is

    K_e={x:g_K(x)+e f(1+a.x)<=1}.                            (2)

It has total first loss D_K=d|T_a(K)|, and every cap through y loses
at least Gamma_d D_K to first order, uniformly over those caps.

## 2. Exact coupled erosions for both input bodies

For every unit n define the continuous positive convex-in-x fields

    Psi_A(n,x)=h_A(n) f(1+[h_M(n)/h_A(n)]a.x),
    Psi_B(n,x)=h_B(n) f(1+[h_M(n)/h_B(n)]a.x).                 (3)

The support ratios are bounded above and below because all three bodies
have an interior origin. Define actual convex input erosions by

    A_e={x:n.x+e Psi_A(n,x)<=h_A(n) for every unit n},
    B_e={x:n.x+e Psi_B(n,x)<=h_B(n) for every unit n}.         (4)

Each set is an intersection of convex sublevel sets. For small e>=0 it
contains a positive homothet of its original body, is contained in that
body, and is compact with the same interior center. These facts also
follow directly from the uniform bounds proved in Section 3.

For x in A_e and x' in B_e, let m=(x+x')/2. Weighted Jensen with weights
h_A(n),h_B(n), and (1), gives

    [Psi_A(n,x)+Psi_B(n,x')]/2
       >=h_M(n) f(1+a.m).                                   (5)

Indeed the weighted average of the two arguments is exactly 1+a.m:
the factors h_M/h_A and h_M/h_B cancel their respective weights. Averaging
the two defining inequalities (4) and using (5) therefore yields

    n.m+e h_M(n)f(1+a.m)<=h_M(n) for every n.

Consequently

    (A_e+B_e)/2 subset M_e
      :={m:g_M(m)+e f(1+a.m)<=1} subset K_e.                 (6)

The last inclusion uses g_K<=g_M. This is exact for every sufficiently
small e, including all originally tight contacts and all boundary points.
It does not require common facet normals, smoothness, or a polyhedral
approximation. Translating the three centered bodies back gives an
actual compatible family at the complete integer base {-1,0,1}.

For the same reason, replacing either input field in (3) by that field
plus ANY nonnegative continuous convex-in-x field preserves (6). This
allows another assigned source in an input fiber; its own projective
field can be added without treating the two losses as disjoint.

## 3. First variation for a continuum of convex inequalities

Here is the nonsmooth justification needed for the input costs. Let L
be any positive convex body with interior origin, and let Psi(n,x)>=0 be
continuous on the unit-normal sphere times a neighborhood of L and convex
in x for each n. Define

    L_e={x:n.x+e Psi(n,x)<=h_L(n) for every n}.               (7)

On a fixed compact neighborhood let C bound Psi/h_L. For small e,

    (1-Ce)L subset L_e subset L.                            (8)

For the first inclusion, evaluate the constraints at (1-Ce)x, x in L;
n.x/h_L<=1 and Psi/h_L<=C. The second uses Psi>=0. In particular the radial
endpoint r_e(u) satisfies

    r_e(u)=rho(u)[1-e delta_e(u)], 0<=delta_e(u)<=C.          (9)

For the boundary point x=rho(u)u let N_L(x) be its supporting unit
normals. Compactness of the sphere, continuity of Psi and h_L, and the
defining maximum in (7) give

    delta_e(u) -> max_(n in N_L(x)) Psi(n,x)/h_L(n).          (10)

For clarity, every active n supplies the lower bound in (10), since its
linear ratio at r_e u is exactly 1-e delta_e. For the reverse bound,
choose a maximizing defining normal at the radial endpoint. Its initial
support gap is nonnegative and tends to zero by (8). Every convergent
subsequence therefore has an active limit normal. The equality at the
radial endpoint bounds delta_e above by that normal's perturbed
Psi/h_L divided by n.x/h_L, which tends to one. This proves the claimed
limit, including nonunique normal cones.

A convex body's boundary has a unique outward normal at surface-almost
every point. Its radial parametrization is Lipschitz, with positive
bounded-away-from-zero cone Jacobian because of the positive inradius
and bounded outer radius. Thus for sphere-almost every u the maximum in
(10) has its single usual normal n_L(x). Dominated convergence in radial
volume integration, using (9), and the boundary cone identity give

    |L|-|L_e|=e D_L+o(e),
    D_L=integral_(boundary L) Psi(n_L(x),x) dH_(d-1)(x).      (11)

The same proof works for d=1 with the two radial points and counting
boundary measure. No differentiability of the gauge or global boundary
normal map is assumed. The maximum over active normals in (10), rather
than an arbitrarily selected support normal, is the correct pointwise
formula at nonsmooth points; its ambiguity is surface-null for (11).

There is also an exact fixed-cap version. If H cuts L properly, its
intersection with boundary L has surface-null cutting boundary, so
the radial layer argument and dominated convergence give

    |L intersect H|-|L_e intersect H|
       =e D_L(H)+o(e),
    D_L(H)=integral_(boundary L intersect int H) Psi dH_(d-1). (12)

The null assertion uses no smoothness: a plane meeting int L has a
full-dimensional convex section in that plane, and its intersection
with boundary L is the relative boundary of that section. That boundary
has zero (d-1)-measure. The d=1 assertion is immediate.

One way to see the radial argument directly is that the removed radial
interval shrinks to x=rho(u)u: its fraction in a fixed H tends to one
or zero according to the strict sign of x's margin. The layer is bounded
by the same integrable radial loss as in (9).

For a full or empty cap, including supporting coincidences, use the
actual status instead:

    D_L(H)=D_L if L subset H;
    D_L(H)=0 if int L intersect H is empty.                  (13)

These formulas are exact because the eroded body is nested. In the second
case both captured d-volumes are zero even if the closed plane contains
a positive-area facet. It would be wrong to insert the closed-boundary
indicator of that facet in (12). Pure integer halfspaces give precisely
the whole-fiber or zero-fiber alternatives in (13).

## 4. The original cap margins and all input cost are retained

Apply (11) to (3), and write

    D_A=integral_boundary A Psi_A,
    D_B=integral_boundary B Psi_B,
    D_K=d|T_a(K)|.

Every term is finite and positive. The total original mixed-volume loss
is exactly

    D_total=D_A+D_K+D_B.                                    (14)

For ONE original ambient closed halfspace H, take its actual restrictions
H_-1,H_0,H_1 in the three translated fibers. Equations (12)--(13) give

    D_total(H)=D_A(H_-1)+D_K(H_0)+D_B(H_1).                  (15)

The input cuts retain the SAME integer tilt and continuous normal as H;
they are not separately optimized or replaced by through-center cuts.
If H contains the assigned middle source, nestedness and the ordinary
projective source theorem give

    D_total(H)>=Gamma_d D_K+D_A(H_-1)+D_B(H_1).             (16)

For a nonvertical cap through that source the source term has the exact
projective identity. For a parallel displaced containing cap, its central
subcap gives the inequality. A purely integer cap containing the source
captures its whole source-fiber loss and also satisfies (16).

There is no assertion D_total<=2D_K, or any other universal cost ratio.
Discarding the two input terms in (16) while discarding their cost in
(14) would be invalid. For a fixed finite actual critical menu, the
quantities in (14)--(15) are its literal first losses; a strict comparison
D_total(H)>beta D_total for every selected row yields descent whenever
the required all-source covers and slack covers persist.

If an input is also an assigned source, add its own projective field as
allowed after (6). By (11)--(13), its cost and every fixed-cap loss add
linearly at first order. Its through-source cap receives its own
Gamma_d payment in addition to any forced input loss. This is an exact
way to account for source/source overlap: the field is summed on the
same boundary, the cost is counted once as that sum, and no disjointness
of losses or source laws is presumed. Several chosen nonnegative rates
give a finite linear comparison for a finite cap menu, but their paying
feasibility is not asserted automatically.

## 5. Exact limitation: at a centroid the coupling is an affine neutral motion

If y is the ordinary centroid of K, choose a=0 and f=1. Then (2)--(4)
reduce exactly to

    A_e=(1-e)A+e y_A,
    K_e=(1-e)K+e y,
    B_e=(1-e)B+e y_B.                                       (17)

Since y=(y_A+y_B)/2, these three maps are the restrictions of ONE ambient
affine map

    (z,x) -> (z,(1-e)x+e[y+z(y_B-y_A)/2]).                   (18)

It preserves the integer base, maps halfspaces bijectively, and multiplies
every fiber volume by (1-e)^d. Therefore the ACTUAL global normalized
depth is unchanged, without a regularity assumption.

For a fixed regular globally critical cap H through the selected source,
its first loss under (18) equals dQ. This can be seen directly from the
critical section/source first moments. With continuous normal u, affine
base margin, and section coareas s_z, divergence writes its contraction
loss as d times its captured volume minus its section margin term.
The section term is a fixed affine function of z that vanishes at the
source base: the contraction-center field in (18) is affine and agrees
with the source. The critical base-moment identity sum s_z(z-p)=0 cancels
it. Thus all regular critical rows have

    D_total(H)=dQ, D_total=dM,
    D_total(H)/D_total=beta.                                (19)

An equivalent argument pulls back H under (18): its first-order change is
a permissible normal variation through the unchanged source, whose
derivative vanishes by genuine criticality. Both arguments retain the
actual integer tilt. Neither equates offset-cap radial boundary flux
with d times the offset-cap volume without its section correction.

The actual complete three-fiber family with radii
(19/20,1,21/20) times T, |T|=9/2, has a globally deepest middle centroid,
an all-proper canonical critical menu, and

    Q=6, M=5409/400, beta=800/1803<4/9.

These all-normal facts are proved in
`candidate f89d52b54ff6950f`.
For d=2, (19) gives total cost 5409/200, every critical-row loss 12, and
exact efficiency 800/1803. Its own source loss is 9 and its own canonical
cap loss is 4, with own efficiency 4/9. The required endpoint losses reduce
the combined ratio to beta. This is a genuine actual critical calibration,
not a volume-only menu or a failure of compatibility.

It refutes a universal Gamma payment for this PARTICULAR explicit coupled
erosion, even though the ordinary source weight pays Gamma exactly.
The family remains above its OC target and has an affine centroid graph,
so it is not an OC counterexample. A useful extension must retain the
extra directional input losses, choose a different compatible coupling,
or use an already solved-class alternative; exact compatibility alone
does not provide the missing quantitative payment. The next two sections
give different exact couplings, including when y is outside M.

## 6. Normal-dependent centers remove the interior-midpoint restriction

For this section restore original, uncentered coordinates. Let y be ANY
interior point of K, without assuming y in M. Use the projective vector
a and convex decreasing f associated to K-y, and put

    H(n)=h_K(n)-n.y>0,
    Delta(n)=h_K(n)-h_M(n)>=0,
    s(n)=h_M(n)-n.y=H(n)-Delta(n).

Let r=min_n H(n)>0, delta=r/4, and choose a continuous cutoff chi(n)
equal to one when Delta<=delta and zero when Delta>=2delta, with
0<=chi<=1. Define normal-dependent centers

    c_A(n)=y+[h_A(n)-h_B(n)]n/2,
    c_B(n)=y-[h_A(n)-h_B(n)]n/2.                            (20)

They have midpoint y and both signed support distances equal s(n).
Where chi>0, s>=r/2>0. Choose arbitrary interior points o_A,o_B of the
input bodies, and define the everywhere positive convex-in-x fields

    Psi_A^c(n,x)=chi(n)s(n) f(1+a.(x-c_A(n)))
                     +(1-chi(n)) h_(A-o_A)(n),
    Psi_B^c(n,x)=chi(n)s(n) f(1+a.(x-c_B(n)))
                     +(1-chi(n)) h_(B-o_B)(n).              (21)

At chi=0 the first term is zero; continuity follows from the compact
normal sphere and bounded arguments. All nonzero coefficients multiplying
f are positive, so these fields satisfy the convexity and continuity
hypotheses of Section 3. Form their input erosions as in (4), now using
the uncentered support inequalities, and keep the original desired K_e.

These erosions are EXACTLY compatible for every sufficiently small e.
Indeed for Delta<=delta one has chi=1. Since c_A+c_B=2y, ordinary Jensen
with equal weights gives

    [Psi_A^c(n,x)+Psi_B^c(n,x')]/2
         >=s(n) f(1+a.(m-y)).

The input inequalities imply

    n.(m-y)+e s(n)f(1+a.(m-y))<=s(n).

Replacing s by H on the left gives at most

    H(n)-Delta(n)[1-e f(1+a.(m-y))]<=H(n)                   (22)

provided e max_M f(1+a.(m-y))<=1. For the remaining normals Delta>delta,
the inputs are nested, so m belongs to M and has original support gap
at least delta. Hence their target inequality is automatic as soon as

    e [max_n H(n)] [max_(m in M) f(1+a.(m-y))]<=delta.       (23)

These two finite bounds prove every defining inequality of K_e for every
midpoint m. The argument includes the cutoff transition band and all
originally active normals. It uses no differentiable support map, facet
enumeration, or approximation. In fact no o(e) hull repair is needed.

The input first costs and fixed-cap losses are exactly (11)--(13) with
Psi_A^c,Psi_B^c. The normal-dependent centers are not claimed to lie inside
the input bodies; only positivity of their signed support distances in
the contact band is used. This is why y outside M causes no difficulty.
No bound on these additional input costs is inferred from (22)--(23).

## 7. An exact one-sided family and a finite cap-sensitive cost test

There is a simpler, possibly more expensive exact construction that also
works for every y in int K. Let b_* minimize a.b on B, and a_* minimize
a.x on A. Such points exist by compactness. Put

    Psi_A^o(n,x)=2H(n) f(1+a.((x+b_*)/2-y)),
    Psi_B^o(n,x')=2H(n) f(1+a.((a_*+x')/2-y)).               (24)

The function f is decreasing on its whole tangent-extended domain. Thus,
for every actual pair x in A,x' in B,

    Psi_A^o(n,x)>=2H(n)f(1+a.(m-y)),
    Psi_B^o(n,x')>=2H(n)f(1+a.(m-y)).                        (25)

For any t in [0,1], erode A with the field t Psi_A^o and B with
(1-t)Psi_B^o. A zero coefficient simply leaves that input unchanged.
Averaging their support inequalities and using (25) gives

    n.(m-y)+e H(n)f(1+a.(m-y))<=h_M(n)-n.y<=H(n).

Therefore the input midpoint is in K_e EXACTLY. There is no contact-band
cutoff and no assumption y in M. Each input field is continuous,
nonnegative and convex in its physical point; small-parameter positivity
of the eroded body follows by translating it to any one interior point
and applying (8).

Write D_A^o,D_B^o and D_A^o(H_-1),D_B^o(H_1) for their actual first costs
and fixed-cap losses computed with (11)--(13). The original total loss
and the loss of any one original ambient cap are exactly

    D(t)=D_K+t D_A^o+(1-t)D_B^o,
    L_H(t)=D_K(H_0)+t D_A^o(H_-1)+(1-t)D_B^o(H_1).           (26)

For a fixed finite actual cap menu, finding t with
L_H(t)>beta D(t) for every row is a literal one-dimensional strict linear
feasibility problem. All coefficients are actual same-cap boundary losses;
supporting full/empty statuses use (13). Thus (26) is a concrete
cap-sensitive coupling test. It does not assert such a t always exists,
nor is it an equivalence with all possible compatible deformations.
With the usual fixed-cover and persistent-slack hypotheses, a feasible t
does give strict actual normalized-depth descent. No minimax or arbitrary
support allocation is used in this sufficient test.

## 8. A paid actual contact calibration beyond the neutral coupling

Return to the exact family in Section 5. Since y=0 and a=0, the normal
contact construction (21) has Delta=0, H=h_T, and both input fields are
h_T. It changes the three radii to

    19/20-e, 1-e, 21/20-e.

The midpoint equality remains exact, all cuts of the canonical critical
branch remain proper for sufficiently small e, and the original all-normal
depth formula gives Q(e)=6(1-e)^2 and
M(e)=5409/400-27e+(27/2)e^2. Thus the first raw loss is12 and total loss27.
Its exact critical
row efficiency is therefore 4/9, and

    L_H-beta D=12-(800/1803)27=12/601>0.                    (27)

The one-sided construction at t=1 instead changes the radii to

    19/20-2e, 1-e, 21/20.

Again the midpoint equality is exact and the same genuine proper branch
persists. Every original critical row loses12 to first order, while
the total loss is 9+18(19/20)=261/10. Hence

    L_H/D=40/87>4/9,
    L_H-beta D=252/601>0.                                  (28)

More explicitly, M(e)=5409/400-(261/10)e+(45/2)e^2 and the true optimized
middle value is again 6(1-e)^2. The OLD ambient caps, with their original
integer tilt held fixed, have mass 6(1-e)^2+4e^2. Thus the fixed-cap
derivative in (28) agrees with the optimized derivative; the finite
second-order difference is retained rather than treating the old caps
as exactly minimizing after deformation.

The endpoint-fiber maxima remain strictly below the middle maximum, so
these are actual global normalized-depth descents, not fixed-source-only
comparisons. Their value is to distinguish compatible couplings: the
balanced support-ratio coupling (3) is exactly neutral here; the
normal-center and one-sided couplings have positive payments (27)--(28)
on the SAME original critical menu. The example is still an already
safe affine-centroid family. It supplies no arbitrary-shape efficiency
theorem or below-target example.

# Perspective-coupled projective erosion and an exact neutrality obstruction

This note realizes the ordinary projective boundary weight through a

Sections of the mathematical submission:
- 1. Data and an explicit interior-midpoint premise
- 2. Exact coupled erosions for both input bodies
- 3. First variation for a continuum of convex inequalities
- 4. The original cap margins and all input cost are retained
